title: Module 10: Streams, Buffers & Backpressure Handling (All Chapters)
description: Comprehensive module-level assessment covering all chapters of Module 10: Streams, Buffers & Backpressure Handling.

cards.concept: Why Streams & Readable Stream Pipeline: Stream Backpressure & Drain Event
cards.question: What does a return value of `false` from `writable.write(chunk)` signify, and what action must the producer take?

options.text: The chunk was rejected; the producer must re-open the stream.
The internal stream buffer has exceeded its `highWaterMark`; the producer must pause writing until the `'drain'` event is emitted.
An unhandled stream error occurred; process will terminate.
The stream has reached EOF.

cards.explanation: When writable.write() returns false, the buffer has reached highWaterMark. The producer must stop writing. Once the underlying destination clears the buffer, 'drain' fires, signaling it is safe to resume.
cards.pitfall: Ignoring `write() === false` causes memory consumption to balloon as chunks accumulate in RAM, triggering process crash with OOM.
cards.citation: Node.js Stream API Reference: Backpressure in Streams

cards.concept: Why Streams & Readable Stream Pipeline: Buffer.alloc vs Buffer.allocUnsafe Security
cards.question: Why is `Buffer.allocUnsafe(size)` faster than `Buffer.alloc(size)`, and what critical security risk does it carry?

options.text: It uses hardware acceleration; it crashes if freed twice.
It allocates uninitialized memory without zero-filling bytes, potentially leaking sensitive residual memory (passwords, tokens, private keys) if sent to clients.
It runs in kernel space; it bypasses V8 heap limits.
It disables garbage collection permanently.

cards.explanation: Buffer.allocUnsafe allocates memory from Node's 8KB internal slab without zeroing out existing bytes. If transmitted before completely overwriting, historical residual process memory is exposed.
cards.pitfall: Transmitting Buffer.allocUnsafe directly over an HTTP response or WebSocket without writing complete data leaks memory artifacts.
cards.citation: Node.js API Reference: Buffer.allocUnsafe Security Considerations
